[
  // State for normal operation
  {
    "state": "NormalOperation",
    "transitions": [
      {
        "trigger": "airLineBlocked",
        "target": "LowPressureAlarm",
        "guard": "airLineBlocked == true",
        "action": "triggerAlarm"
      },
      {
        "trigger": "O2LineBlocked",
        "target": "LowPressureAlarm",
        "guard": "O2LineBlocked == true",
        "action": "triggerAlarm"
      },
      {
        "trigger": "inspiratoryPressureBelowThreshold",
        "target": "LowPressureAlarm",
        "guard": "inspiratoryPressure == -4",
        "action": "triggerAlarm"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "state": "LowPressureAlarm",
    "transitions": [
      {
        "trigger": "alarmResolved",
        "target": "NormalOperation",
        "guard": "false",
        "action": "resetAlarm"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "state": "ControllerUnresponsive",
    "transitions": [
      {
        "trigger": "apneaTimeElapsed",
        "target": "ControllerUnresponsive",
        "guard": "apneaTimeElapsed >= 0.5",
        "action": "triggerAlarm"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "state": "Overpressure",
    "transitions": [
      {
        "trigger": "pressureAboveThreshold",
        "target": "OverpressureAlarm",
        "guard": "pressure >= 60",
        "action": "triggerAlarm"
      }
    ]
  },
  {
    "state": "OverpressureAlarm",
    "transitions": [
      {
        "trigger": "alarmResolved",
        "target": "NormalOperation",
        "guard": "false",
        "action": "resetAlarm"
      }
    ]
  }
]
```

Please note that the Statecharts notation provided above is a simplified textual representation. In practice, Statecharts would be visualized using a specialized tool that supports the graphical representation of states, transitions, events, and guards. The actual Statecharts would include more detailed states and transitions to handle mode switching, lifecycle behavior, and guard conditions for each transition. The Statecharts would also include additional states and transitions to cover boundary values and error paths as required by the test suite.

Remember, the Statecharts and JSON test cases should be designed to ensure 100% state coverage and 100% transition coverage, with guard conditions tested under both True and False values. The Statecharts should also be grounded, meaning all concrete values should come from the requirement text, and any unspecified values should be clearly marked as "as specified." The above JSON test cases and Statechart structure aim to meet these criteria, but the full Statechart would need to be visualized using a Statechart tool for complete accuracy and validation.
